heading_en: Whether virtue or fortune was the greater cause of Rome's empire
thesis: Rome's empire was won not by fortune alone, as Plutarch and even Livy suggest, but by extraordinary virtue and prudence mixed with fortune, visible in the ordering of its wars.
thesis_quote: chi considererà bene l’ordine di queste guerre, ed il modo del procedere loro, vi vedrà dentro mescolate con la fortuna una virtù e prudenza grandissima

propositions.statement: When a prince or people attains such reputation that every neighbor fears to attack it on its own, each will attack only when forced, leaving the power free to choose its wars and lull the rest.
propositions.quote: come uno principe e uno popolo viene in tanta riputazione, che ciascuno principe e popolo vicino abbia di per sé paura ad assaltarlo e ne tema, sempre interverrà che ciascuno d’essi mai lo assalterà, se non necessitato

propositions.statement: Rome never had two very powerful wars at the same time; one always arose as the other was extinguished.
propositions.quote: mai non intervenne che eglino avessero due potentissime guerre in uno medesimo tempo: anzi parve sempre che, o, nel nascere dell’una, l’altra si spegnesse

propositions.statement: Had two of those powers joined forces while fresh, the ruin of the Roman republic would surely have followed.
propositions.quote: che se due di queste potenze intere si fossero, quando erano fresche, accozzate insieme, senza dubbio si può facilmente conietturare che ne sarebbe seguito la rovina della romana Republica

propositions.statement: The Romans always secured some friend in a new province to serve as ladder and gate for entering and holding it.
propositions.quote: sempre s’ingegnarono avere nelle provincie nuove qualche amico che fussi scala o porta a salirvi o entrarvi, o mezzo a tenerla

episodes.description: The sequence of Rome's wars: first the Aequi and Volsci, then the Samnites, the Latin revolt (with Samnite help for Rome), the Tuscans, Pyrrhus, and finally Carthage, never two great wars at once.
episodes.quote: mentre che combatterno con gli Equi e con i Volsci, mai, mentre che questi popoli furono potenti, non scesero contro di loro altre genti

episodes.description: After the First Punic War all the Gauls on both sides of the Alps conspired against Rome and were slaughtered between Populonia and Pisa.
episodes.quote: intra Populonia e Pisa, dove è oggi la torre a San Vincenti, furono con massima strage superati

episodes.description: The Carthaginians, powerful but distant, never thought of attacking Rome or aiding the Samnites and Tuscans, even seeking Roman friendship until it was too late.
episodes.quote: fece che non pensarono mai di assaltare quello, né di soccorrere i Sanniti ed i Toscani

episodes.description: Rome entered provinces through local friends: the Capuans into Samnium, Camertines in Tuscany, Mamertines in Sicily, Saguntines in Spain, Masinissa in Africa, Aetolians in Greece.
episodes.quote: per il mezzo de’ Capuani entrarono in Sannio, de’ Camertini in Toscana, de’ Mamertini in Sicilia, de’ Saguntini in Spagna

notes: Livy invoked ('E pare che a questa opinione si accosti Livio') as leaning toward the fortune thesis Machiavelli rejects.

heading_en: The peoples Rome fought and how obstinately they defended their liberty
thesis: Nothing made Roman conquest harder than the ancient peoples' love of liberty, for only free cities pursuing the common good grow in dominion and wealth.
thesis_quote: Nessuna cosa fe’ più faticoso a’ Romani superare i popoli d’intorno e parte delle provincie discosto, quanto lo amore che in quelli tempi molti popoli avevano alla libertà

propositions.statement: Not private but common good makes cities great, and the common good is observed only in republics.
propositions.quote: non il bene particulare, ma il bene comune è quello che fa grandi le città. E senza dubbio, questo bene comune non è osservato se non nelle republiche

propositions.statement: As soon as a tyranny arises over a free polity, the least evil is that the city stops growing; usually it goes backward.
propositions.quote: subito che nasce una tirannide sopra uno vivere libero, il manco male che ne resulti a quelle città è non andare più innanzi

propositions.statement: Christian education, prizing humility over worldly honor, has made men weaker than the ancients, whose religion made them fierce in action.
propositions.quote: avendoci la nostra religione mostro la verità e la vera via, ci fa stimare meno l’onore del mondo: onde i Gentili, stimandolo assai, ed avendo posto in quello il sommo bene, erano nelle azioni loro più feroci

propositions.statement: Of all hard servitudes, the hardest is subjection to a republic, which is more durable and aims to enervate all other bodies to swell its own.
propositions.quote: E di tutte le servitù dure, quella è durissima che ti sottomette a una republica

episodes.description: The Tuscans refused to aid Veii against Rome so long as the Veientes, who had made themselves a king, lived under him.
episodes.quote: deliberarono di non dare aiuto a’ Veienti, infino a tanto che vivessono sotto il re

episodes.description: On the death of Hieronymus of Syracuse his army, about to avenge him, was calmed entirely by the cry of liberty in the city.
episodes.quote: come ei sentì che in Siracusa si gridava libertà, allettato da quel nome, si quietò tutto

episodes.description: In Corcyra during the Peloponnesian war the popular party imprisoned the nobles and killed them all, crushing the last under the ruins of their prison.
episodes.quote: il popolo, a questo romore fatto uno concorso, scoperse la parte superiore di quel luogo, e quegli con quelle rovine suffocò

episodes.description: The Samnites, while free, resisted Rome for forty-six years until the consulship of Papirius Cursor the younger despite repeated defeats.
episodes.quote: potessono infino al tempo di Papirio Cursore consolo, figliuolo del primo Papirio, resistere a’ Romani

episodes.description: Reduced to servitude, the Samnites sent envoys begging Hannibal for help because they could barely defend themselves against one Roman legion at Nola.
episodes.quote: sendo i Sanniti oppressi da una legione di uomini che era in Nola, mandarono oratori ad Annibale, a pregarlo che gli soccorressi

heading_en: Rome became great by ruining neighboring cities and freely admitting foreigners to its honors
thesis: A city that would build empire must fill itself with inhabitants, by love (welcoming foreigners) and by force (destroying neighboring cities and transplanting their people).
thesis_quote: si debbono con ogni industria ingegnare di farla piena di abitatori; perché, sanza questa abbondanza di uomini, mai non riuscirà di fare grande una città

propositions.statement: There are two ways to populate a city: by love and by force.
propositions.quote: Questo si fa in due modi: per amore e per forza

propositions.statement: A small republic cannot seize cities or kingdoms stronger than itself; like a thin trunk bearing a thick branch, any small wind breaks it.
propositions.quote: una republica piccola non può occupare città né regni che sieno più validi né più grossi di lei

propositions.statement: Sparta and Athens, though heavily armed and excellently ordered, never reached Roman greatness because they kept their bodies small.
propositions.quote: essendo dua republiche armatissime, ed ordinate di ottime leggi, nondimeno non si condussono alla grandezza dello Imperio romano

episodes.description: By the time of the sixth king Rome held eighty thousand men capable of bearing arms, grown by destroying neighbors and receiving foreigners.
episodes.quote: nel tempo del sesto re, in Roma abitavano ottantamila uomini da portare arme

episodes.description: Livy's dictum that Rome grows on the ruins of Alba epitomizes the method.
episodes.quote: Il che dimostra Tito Livio in due parole, quando disse: «Crescit interea Roma Albae ruinis»

episodes.description: Lycurgus barred foreigners from Sparta, even instituting leather money to deter traders, so Sparta never exceeded twenty thousand men and, after Thebes rebelled, lost all its Greek conquests.
episodes.quote: ordinò che in quella sua republica si spendesse monete di cuoio, per tor via a ciascuno il disiderio di venirvi

institutions: admission of foreigners to civic honors
notes: Chapter opens and closes with the same Latin tag from Livy 1.30.

heading_en: Republics have had three modes of expansion
thesis: Of the three modes of expansion — a league of equal republics, making companions while keeping command, and making outright subjects — the Roman mode of companions under one head is the only true path to great empire.
thesis_quote: le republiche hanno tenuti tre modi circa lo ampliare

propositions.statement: Making immediate subjects is wholly useless: Sparta and Athens were ruined precisely by acquiring dominion they could not hold.
propositions.quote: De’ quali tre modi, questo ultimo è al tutto inutile; come si vide ch’ei fu nelle soprascritte due republiche: le quali non rovinarono per altro, se non per avere acquistato quel dominio che le non potevano tenere

propositions.statement: The league mode has a fixed limit, never exceeded in any example, of about twelve or fourteen communities, after which it seeks no further dominion.
propositions.quote: simile modo di procedere ha un termine fisso, il quale non ci è esemplo che mostri che si sia trapassato: e questo è di aggiugnere a dodici o quattordici comunità

propositions.statement: A republic that wishes to expand can hold no other mode than Rome's, experience having shown none more certain or true.
propositions.quote: né può tenere altro modo una republica che voglia ampliare; perché la esperienza non ce ne ha mostro nessuno più certo o più vero

episodes.description: The ancient Tuscans, a league of twelve equal cities including Chiusi, Veii, Arezzo, Fiesole and Volterra, ruled Italy from the Tiber to the Alps before losing Lombardy to the Gauls.
episodes.quote: furono dodici città, tra le quali era Chiusi, Veio, Arezzo, Fiesole, Volterra, e simili: i quali per via di lega governavano lo Imperio loro

episodes.description: Rome's Italian companions, having helped subjugate the provinces with their own blood, found themselves suddenly ringed by Roman subjects, and when they conspired against Rome they lost and became subjects themselves.
episodes.quote: quegli compagni di Roma che erano in Italia, si trovarono in un tratto cinti da’ sudditi romani, ed oppressi da una grossissima città come era Roma

episodes.description: At the parley between Philip of Macedon and Titus Quinctius Flamininus, Philip reproached the Aetolian praetor for Aetolian greed and faithlessness in serving both sides for pay.
episodes.quote: venendo a parlamento Filippo re di Macedonia con Tito Quinzio Flaminio, e ragionando d’accordo alla presenza d’uno pretore degli Etoli

episodes.description: Today only the Swiss and the Swabian league imitate the ancient league mode of the Tuscans, Achaeans and Aetolians.
episodes.quote: E quanto alle leghe, si trovano solo i Svizzeri e la lega di Svezia che gli imita

institutions: seat of empire and title of command
notes: The Flamininus parley is in Livy book 32-33, outside Livy I-X, so no candidate given.

heading_en: Changes of sects and languages, with floods and plagues, extinguish the memory of things
thesis: The memory of the past is extinguished partly by human causes — changes of religions and languages — and partly by heaven, through flood, plague and famine that nearly wipe out mankind.
thesis_quote: queste memorie de’ tempi per diverse cagioni si spengano: delle quali, parte vengono dagli uomini, parte dal cielo

propositions.statement: When a new sect arises, its first effort, to gain reputation, is to extinguish the old one, and it succeeds easily when its founders speak a different language.
propositions.quote: quando e’ surge una setta nuova, cioè una religione nuova, il primo studio suo è, per darsi riputazione, estinguere la vecchia

propositions.statement: Since sects change two or three times in five or six thousand years, memory of things done before is lost, and surviving traces are dismissed as fable.
propositions.quote: queste sètte in cinque o in seimila anni variano due o tre volte, si perde la memoria delle cose fatte innanzi a quel tempo

propositions.statement: When provinces are overfull and human cunning at its height, nature necessarily purges the world through flood, plague or famine, as in simple bodies.
propositions.quote: conviene di necessità che il mondo si purghi per uno de’ tre modi; acciocché gli uomini, sendo divenuti pochi e battuti, vivino più comodamente

episodes.description: The Christian sect, under St. Gregory and other church heads, obstinately persecuted pagan memory, burning the works of poets and historians and destroying images.
episodes.quote: e’ perseguitarono tutte le memorie antiche, ardendo le opere de’ poeti e degli istorici, ruinando le imagini

episodes.description: Tuscany, once powerful and full of religion and virtue with its own customs and language, was so extinguished by Roman power that only the memory of its name remains.
episodes.quote: già la Toscana potente, piena di religione e di virtù, aveva i suoi costumi e la sua lingua patria: il che tutto è suto spento dalla potenza romana

notes: Largely theoretical chapter; mentions Diodorus Siculus and Procopius-adjacent themes elsewhere.

heading_en: How the Romans proceeded in making war
thesis: The Romans made their wars short and massive, ending them with quick decisive battles, land confiscations and frontier colonies, so that war enriched rather than impoverished the state.
thesis_quote: fu in prima di fare le guerre, come dicano i Franciosi, corte e grosse

propositions.statement: In acquiring and holding one must think not to spend but to do everything to the public profit.
propositions.quote: È necessario dunque, e nello acquistare e nel mantenere, pensare di non spendere; anzi fare ogni cosa con utilità del publico suo

propositions.statement: Colonies placed on conquered frontiers guarded Roman borders at no public expense while profiting the colonists.
propositions.quote: la quale posta in su le frontiere di coloro veniva ad essere guardia de’ confini romani, con utile di essi coloni

propositions.statement: The consuls' ambition to triumph within their one-year term kept wars short even after soldiers' pay allowed longer campaigns.
propositions.quote: gli tenne, circa il fare le guerre brevi oltra a il loro naturale uso, l’ambizione de’ Consoli

episodes.description: All Roman wars from the city's beginning to the siege of Veii — against Latins, Samnites and Tuscans — were dispatched in six, ten or twenty days by immediate pitched battle.
episodes.quote: tutte si vedranno ispedite, quale in sei, quale in dieci, quale in venti dì

episodes.description: At the siege of Veii the Romans instituted pay for their soldiers so as to be able to wage war at length and at a distance.
episodes.quote: il che fu dopo la ossidione de’ Veienti; dove, per potere fare guerra lungamente, gli ordinarono di pagare i soldati

heading_en: How much land the Romans gave per colonist
thesis: Roman land distributions to colonists were everywhere sparing, so as to send more men as guards and keep colonists as poor abroad as citizens were at home.
thesis_quote: Giudicasi che ad ogni modo ed in ogni luogo la distribuzione fussi parca

propositions.statement: Distribution was sparing first to send more men as garrison, and because those living poor at home would not let their colonists abound abroad.
propositions.quote: prima, per potere mandare più uomini, sendo quelli diputati per guardia di quel paese; dipoi perché, vivendo loro poveri a casa, non era ragionevole che volessono che i loro uomini abbondassino troppo fuora

propositions.statement: The Romans judged that not abundant but well-cultivated land sufficed.
propositions.quote: non lo assai terreno, ma il bene cultivato, bastasse

propositions.statement: Every colony must have public fields for pasturing livestock and woods for firewood, without which it cannot be ordered.
propositions.quote: È necessario bene, che tutta la colonia abbi campi publici dove ciascuno possa pascere il suo bestiame

episodes.description: After Veii was taken the Romans sent a colony there and distributed to each colonist three iugera and seven unciae of land.
episodes.quote: preso Veio, e’ vi mandarono una colonia, e distribuirono a ciascuno tre iugeri e sètte once di terra

notes: The text has a lacuna after 'che sono, al modo nostro....' where the modern equivalent of the measure is left blank.

heading_en: Why peoples leave their native lands and flood other countries
thesis: Besides wars of ambition there are wars of whole migrating peoples, driven by famine or war to seize and wholly possess new lands; these are the cruelest and most terrifying wars.
thesis_quote: quando uno popolo intero con tutte le sue famiglie si lieva d’uno luogo, necessitato o dalla fame o dalla guerra, e va a cercare nuova sede e nuova provincia

propositions.statement: Wars of ambition, however dangerous, do not expel a province's inhabitants, since the victor is content with obedience and usually leaves laws, homes and goods.
propositions.quote: Le quali guerre sono pericolose, ma non cacciano al tutto gli abitatori d’una provincia; perché e’ basta, al vincitore, solo la ubbidienza de’ popoli

propositions.statement: Peoples driven out by ultimate necessity are most formidable and can be withstood only by good arms.
propositions.quote: Sono, pertanto, questi popoli formidolosissimi, sendo cacciati da una ultima necessità; e se e’ non riscontrano buone armi, non mai saranno sostenuti

propositions.statement: The great migrating hordes have almost all come from Scythia, whose cold poor lands cannot feed their many men.
propositions.quote: Escono i popoli grossi, e sono usciti quasi tutti, de’ paesi di Scizia; luoghi freddi e poveri

episodes.description: Overpopulated Gaul sent out part of its people under Bellovesus and Sicovesus; Bellovesus crossed into Italy, took Lombardy from the Tuscans, and thence came the first Gallic war on Rome.
episodes.quote: elessono, per capitani di quegli che si avevano a partire, Belloveso e Sicoveso, duoi re de’ Franciosi: de’ quali Belloveso venne in Italia, e Sicoveso passò in Ispagna

episodes.description: The first of Rome's three migration wars: the capture of Rome by the Gauls who had earlier seized Lombardy.
episodes.quote: La prima fu quella quando Roma fu presa, la quale fu occupata da quei Franciosi che avevano tolto, come di sopra si disse, la Lombardia a’ Toscani

episodes.description: The second: after the First Punic War the Romans killed more than two hundred thousand Gauls between Piombino and Pisa.
episodes.quote: quella che fecero dopo la prima guerra cartaginese, quando intra Piombino e Pisa ammazzarono più che dugentomila Franciosi

episodes.description: The third: the Germans and Cimbri, having beaten several Roman armies, came into Italy and were defeated by Marius.
episodes.quote: quando i Tedeschi e’ Cimbri vennero in Italia: i quali, avendo vinti più eserciti romani, furono vinti da Mario

episodes.description: When Roman virtue failed, the empire was destroyed by similar peoples — Goths, Vandals and the like — who occupied the whole western empire.
episodes.quote: fu quello imperio destrutto da simili popoli: i quali furono Gotti, Vandali, e simili, che occuparono tutto lo Imperio occidentale

episodes.description: The Maurusii of Syria, unable to resist the invading Hebrews, abandoned their country for Africa, driving out its inhabitants, as Procopius's column inscriptions attest.
episodes.quote: levatisi con loro famiglie, se ne andarono in Africa, dove posero la loro sedia, cacciando via quelli abitatori che in quegli luoghi trovarono

episodes.description: Moses occupied part of Syria and renamed it Judea, as new occupiers rename provinces.
episodes.quote: Moisè ancora chiamò Giudea quella parte di Soria occupata da lui

episodes.description: Small displaced groups like Aeneas, Dido and the Massilians seized places by art rather than violence, maintaining themselves with the consent of neighbors.
episodes.quote: come si vede che fece Enea, Didone, i Massiliesi e simili; i quali tutti, per consentimento de’ vicini, dov’e’ posono, poterono mantenervisi

notes: Also cites Sallust (end of the Jugurthine War) and Procopius.

heading_en: What causes commonly make wars arise among the powerful
thesis: Wars among powerful states arise either by chance, as the Roman-Samnite war did, or are deliberately engineered by one who wants war, typically by attacking the friend of his intended enemy.
thesis_quote: è una cagione comune che nasce infra tutti i principati potenti. La quale cagione o la viene a caso o la è fatta nascere da colui che disidera muovere la guerra

propositions.statement: To war on a prince with whom treaties stand, one attacks his friend instead: either he reacts, giving the desired war, or his failure to defend a client exposes his weakness or faithlessness.
propositions.quote: con altra giustificazione e con altro colore assalterò io uno suo amico che lui proprio

propositions.statement: A city that cannot defend itself but wants defense at all costs should give itself freely to the power it designs as its defender.
propositions.quote: darsi liberamente a quello che tu disegni che ti difenda

propositions.statement: Rome, having empire and glory and not quiet as its end, could not refuse the Campanian enterprise.
propositions.quote: avendo Roma per fine lo imperio e la gloria, e non la quiete, non poteva ricusare questa impresa

episodes.description: The Samnite war arose by chance when the oppressed Campanians gave themselves to Rome, forcing the Romans to defend them as subjects against their Samnite allies.
episodes.quote: sendo i Campani oppressati, e ricorrendo a Roma fuora della opinione de’ Romani e de’ Sanniti, furono forzati, dandosi i Campani ai Romani, come cosa loro defendergli

episodes.description: The First Punic War likewise began by chance from Rome's defense of the Messinesi in Sicily.
episodes.quote: Questa medesima cagione dette principio alla prima guerra contro ai Cartaginesi, per la defensione che i Romani presono de’ Messinesi in Sicilia

episodes.description: Hannibal attacked Rome's Saguntine friends in Spain not to harm them but to provoke Roman arms and gain occasion to pass into Italy.
episodes.quote: Annibale capitano cartaginese assaltò i Saguntini amici de’ Romani in Ispagna, non per offendere quelli, ma per muovere l’armi romane

episodes.description: The Florentines gave themselves to King Robert of Naples, who, unwilling to defend them as friends, defended them as subjects against Castruccio of Lucca.
episodes.quote: i Fiorentini a il re Ruberto di Napoli: il quale non gli volendo difendere come amici, gli difese poi come sudditi contro alle forze di Castruccio da Lucca

heading_en: Money is not the sinews of war, contrary to common opinion
thesis: Good soldiers, not gold, are the sinews of war: gold cannot find good soldiers, but good soldiers can always find gold.
thesis_quote: non l’oro, come grida la comune opinione, essere il nervo della guerra, ma i buoni soldati: perché l’oro non è sufficiente a trovare i buoni soldati, ma i buoni soldati sono bene sufficienti a trovare l’oro

propositions.statement: A prince will always deceive himself if he measures his forces by money, terrain or men's goodwill while lacking arms of his own.
propositions.quote: ogni volta s’ingannerà, quando le misuri o dai danari, o dal sito, o dalla benivolenza degli uomini, mancando, dall’altra parte, d’armi proprie

propositions.statement: Money not only fails to defend you but makes you plundered the sooner.
propositions.quote: I danari ancora, non solo non ti difendono, ma ti fanno predare più presto

propositions.statement: Many necessities, of which shortage of money is only one, force a captain to battle against his intention.
propositions.quote: Sono, adunque, molte necessitadi che fanno a un capitano fuor della sua intenzione pigliare partito di azzuffarsi, intra le quali qualche volta può essere la carestia de’ danari

episodes.description: The Spartan king, lacking money against Antipater, was forced to battle and beaten, whereas a few days' delay would have brought news of Alexander's death and victory without fighting (Quintus Curtius).
episodes.quote: per difetto di danari, il re di Sparta fu necessitato azzuffarsi, e fu rotto

episodes.description: Shown Croesus's innumerable treasure, Solon judged him no more powerful for it, since war is made with iron, not gold.
episodes.quote: gli rispose Solone, che per quello e’ non lo giudicava più potente; perché la guerra si faceva con il ferro e non con l’oro

episodes.description: The king of Macedon displayed his gold and silver to Gallic envoys to frighten them; the Gauls broke the nearly settled peace out of desire to seize that gold.
episodes.quote: quel re, per mostrare la potenza sua e per sbigottirli, mostrò loro oro ed ariento assai

episodes.description: The Venetians recently lost their whole state although their treasury was still full of treasure.
episodes.quote: I Viniziani, pochi anni sono, avendo ancora lo erario loro pieno di tesoro, perderno tutto lo stato

episodes.description: Livy, debating whether Alexander would have beaten Rome, names three necessities of war — many good soldiers, prudent captains and good fortune — never mentioning money.
episodes.quote: mostra essere tre cose necessarie nella guerra; assai soldati e buoni, capitani prudenti, e buona fortuna

episodes.description: The Capuans, measuring their power by money rather than soldiers, aided the Sidicini and after two defeats had to make themselves tributaries of Rome.
episodes.quote: preso ch’egli ebbero partito di aiutargli, dopo due rotte furono constretti farsi tributari de’ Romani, se si vollono salvare

episodes.description: Modern proofs: Duke Charles was beaten by the Swiss, and the Pope and Florentines together could not easily beat Francesco Maria in the war of Urbino, despite money.
episodes.quote: il duca Carlo arebbe vinti i Svizzeri; e pochi giorni sono, il Papa ed i Fiorentini insieme non arebbono avuta difficultà in vincere Francesco Maria

episodes.description: Hasdrubal, caught in the Marches by Claudius Nero and the other consul, had to choose between flight and battle, and chose battle.
episodes.quote: come intervenne a Asdrubale, quando nella Marca fu assaltato da Claudio Nerone, insieme con l’altro console romano

notes: Also cites Quintus Curtius and Pericles's advice to the Athenians.

heading_en: It is not prudent to ally with a prince who has more reputation than strength
thesis: Leagues with princes who lack the proximity or forces to help bring more fame than aid to those who trust in them.
thesis_quote: le leghe che si fanno coi principi, che non abbino o commodità di aiutarti per la distanza del sito, o forze da farlo per suo disordine o altra sua cagione, arrecono più fama che aiuto

propositions.statement: Alliances with distant or disordered princes yield reputation, not protection, to those who rely on them.
propositions.quote: le leghe che si fanno coi principi, che non abbino o commodità di aiutarti per la distanza del sito, o forze da farlo per suo disordine o altra sua cagione, arrecono più fama che aiuto

propositions.statement: Men of little prudence, unable to defend themselves, nevertheless undertake to defend others.
propositions.quote: non sappiendo né potendo difendere sé medesimi, vogliono prendere impresa di difendere altrui

episodes.description: Livy's verdict on the Sidicini trusting Campanian aid: the Campanians brought a name rather than forces to their protection.
episodes.quote: «Campani magis nomen in auxilium Sidicinorum, quam vires ad praesidium attulerunt»

episodes.description: In 1479, attacked by the Pope and the king of Naples, the Florentines drew from their French friendship a name rather than protection.
episodes.quote: nel 1479, il Papa ed il re di Napoli gli assaltarono: ché, essendo amici del re di Francia, trassono di quella amicizia «magis nomen, quam praesidium»

episodes.description: The Tarentine ambassadors demanded peace between Rome and the Samnites; the Roman consul, laughing, had battle sounded in their presence.
episodes.quote: il Console, ridendosi di questa proposta, alla presenza di detti ambasciadori fece sonare a battaglia

notes: Also warns against enterprises trusting Emperor Maximilian.

heading_en: Whether, fearing attack, it is better to begin war or to await it
thesis: A prince whose people are armed and ordered for war should await a powerful war at home; one with unarmed subjects should carry war as far from home as he can.
thesis_quote: quel principe che ha i suoi popoli armati ed ordinati alla guerra, aspetti sempre in casa una guerra potente e pericolosa, e non la vadia a rincontrare

propositions.statement: He whose subjects are unarmed and country unused to war should keep the war far from home, since his strength lies in money, which home war cuts off.
propositions.quote: quello che ha i suoi sudditi disarmati, ed il paese inusitato alla guerra, se le discosti sempre da casa il più che può

propositions.statement: Soldiers in another's country are more compelled to fight, and that necessity makes virtue.
propositions.quote: i suoi soldati, per trovarsi nel paese d’altrui, sono più necessitati a combattere; e quella necessità fa virtù

propositions.statement: Awaiting at home you risk all your forces but not all your fortune; going abroad you risk all your fortune but not all your forces.
propositions.quote: tanto che tu vieni ad arristiare tutte le forze, e non tutta la fortuna; e, discostandoti, arrischi tutta la fortuna, e non tutte le forze

propositions.statement: Had Rome suffered its three Hannibalic defeats in France instead of Italy, it would without doubt have been finished.
propositions.quote: se i Romani avessono avute in tanto spazio di tempo quelle tre rotte in Francia ch’egli ebbero in Italia da Annibale, sanza dubbio erano spacciati

episodes.description: Croesus, against the others' opinion, advised Cyrus to cross into queen Tomyris's realm to attack the Massagetae in their own country.
episodes.quote: Creso, contro alla opinione degli altri, disse che si andasse a trovare lei

episodes.description: Hannibal advised Antiochus that the Romans could be beaten only in Italy, where their fount of men and wealth could be dried up.
episodes.quote: ei mostra come i Romani non si potevano vincere se non in Italia

episodes.description: Agathocles, unable to sustain the war at home, attacked the Carthaginians in Africa and reduced them to asking for peace.
episodes.quote: Agatocle che, non potendo sostenere la guerra di casa, assaltò i Cartaginesi che gliene facevano, e gli ridusse a domandare pace

episodes.description: Scipio attacked Africa to lift the war from Italy.
episodes.quote: Allega Scipione che, per levare la guerra di Italia, assaltò la Africa

episodes.description: The Athenians prospered while warring near home but lost their liberty when they took their armies to Sicily.
episodes.quote: come si discostarono, ed andarono con gli eserciti in Sicilia, perderono la libertà

episodes.description: The fable of Antaeus, king of Libya, invincible while he awaited Hercules within his own borders but lost when drawn away from the earth, his mother.
episodes.quote: Anteo, re di Libia, assaltato da Ercole Egizio, fu insuperabile mentre che lo aspettò dentro a’ confini del suo regno

episodes.description: Dying Ferdinand of Naples counseled his son Alfonso to await Charles VIII inside the kingdom; the advice was ignored, and army and state were lost without a battle.
episodes.quote: fu ch’egli aspettasse il nimico dentro a il regno; e per cosa del mondo non traesse forze fuora dello stato suo

episodes.description: The Florentines were helpless against Castruccio's war at home yet later boldly attacked the duke of Milan far away — brave in distant wars, cowardly in near ones.
episodes.quote: tanta virtù mostrarono nelle guerre longinque, e tanta viltà nelle propinque

episodes.description: The Cimbri broke a Roman army in Germany where Rome had no remedy, but once in Italy, facing Rome's united forces, they were destroyed.
episodes.quote: I Cimbri ruppono uno esercito romano nella Magna, né vi ebbono i Romani rimedio

heading_en: One rises from low to great fortune more by fraud than by force
thesis: Men of small fortune rarely or never reach great rank without force and fraud; force alone never suffices, but fraud alone can, and republics too must use it until they are powerful.
thesis_quote: rado, o non mai, intervenga che gli uomini di piccola fortuna venghino a gradi grandi, sanza la forza e sanza la fraude

propositions.statement: Force alone is never found sufficient, but fraud alone will be found sufficient.
propositions.quote: Né credo si truovi mai che la forza sola basti, ma si troverrà bene che la fraude sola basterà

propositions.statement: What princes must do at the beginnings of their growth, republics too must do until they have become powerful and force alone suffices.
propositions.quote: quel che sono necessitati fare i principi ne’ principii degli augumenti loro, sono ancora necessitate a fare le republiche, infino che le siano diventate potenti

propositions.statement: Fraud is the less blameworthy the more it is covered, as Rome's was.
propositions.quote: la quale è meno vituperabile quanto è più coperta, come fu questa de’ Romani

episodes.description: Xenophon's Cyrus rose through deceit: his first expedition against the king of Armenia was full of fraud, and he deceived his uncle Cyaxares in many ways.
episodes.quote: la prima ispedizione che fe’ fare a Ciro contro al re di Armenia è piena di fraude

episodes.description: Giangaleazzo Visconti took the state and empire of Lombardy from his uncle Bernabò by fraud.
episodes.quote: come fece Giovan Galeazzo per tôrre lo stato e lo imperio di Lombardia a messer Bernabò suo zio

episodes.description: Rome's greatest early fraud was making 'companions' of the Latins and neighbors, who under that name made themselves slaves with their own arms and blood.
episodes.quote: Né poté usare, nel principio, il maggiore inganno, che pigliare il modo, discorso di sopra da noi, di farsi compagni; perché sotto questo nome se gli fece servi

episodes.description: The Latins recognized the deception only after Rome's double defeat of the Samnites, as the Latin praetor Annius Setinus declared in their council.
episodes.quote: «Nam si etiam nunc sub umbra foederis aequi servitutem pati possumus etc.»

notes: Also cites Xenophon's Cyropaedia and the careers of Philip of Macedon and Agathocles.

heading_en: Men often deceive themselves believing humility conquers pride
thesis: Humility toward insolent enemies not only does not help but harms: Roman patience only increased Latin arrogance, so a prince should never yield from fear of force.
thesis_quote: Vedesi molte volte come l’umiltà non solamente non giova ma nuoce, massimamente usandola con gli uomini insolenti

propositions.statement: It is almost always better to let a thing be taken from you by force than by the fear of force.
propositions.quote: gli è meglio, quasi sempre, sendosi condotta la cosa in termine che tu non la possa lasciare nel modo detto, lasciarsela tôrre con le forze, che con la paura delle forze

propositions.statement: Yielding from fear does not remove the war: the adversary, esteeming you less, will want more, while your defenders grow colder.
propositions.quote: se tu la lasci con la paura, lo fai per levarti la guerra, ed il più delle volte non te la lievi

propositions.statement: With several enemies, it is always prudent to give something back to one of them, even after war has broken out, to regain him and split him from the confederates.
propositions.quote: rendere delle cose che tu possedessi a alcuno di loro per riguadagnarselo, ancora che fussi di già scoperta la guerra, e per ismembrarlo dagli altri confederati tuoi nimici, fia sempre partito prudente

episodes.description: When the Samnites complained of Latin attacks, Rome, not wishing to irritate the Latins, declined to forbid the war — which emboldened the Latins and made them open enemies sooner, as Annius's speech on Roman patience shows.
episodes.quote: i Romani non vollono proibire ai Latini tale guerra, disiderando non gli irritare: il che non solamente non gli irritò ma gli fece diventare più animosi

notes: Livy is invoked as 'lo istorico nostro' and quoted in Latin (Annius's speech, Livy 8.4) but not named.

heading_en: Weak states are always ambiguous in resolving, and slow deliberations are always harmful
thesis: In every consultation one must come to a definite resolution, for ambiguity and slow deliberation harm republics; once the mind is fixed on what to do, the words are easily found.
thesis_quote: in ogni consulta è bene venire allo individuo di quello che si ha a diliberare, e non stare sempre in ambiguo né in su lo incerto della cosa

propositions.statement: Once the mind is firm and the course resolved, it is easy to find the words to fit the deeds.
propositions.quote: fermo una volta l’animo, e diliberato quello sia da esequire, è facil cosa trovarvi le parole

propositions.statement: Slow and late deliberations are no less harmful than ambiguous ones, especially those in favor of a friend: they help no one and hurt oneself.
propositions.quote: Non sono meno nocive ancora le diliberazioni lente e tarde, che le ambigue; massime quelle che si hanno a diliberare in favore di alcuno amico

propositions.statement: Such deliberations proceed either from weakness of spirit and forces or from the malignity of the deliberators.
propositions.quote: Queste diliberazioni così fatte procedono o da debolezza d’animo e di forze, o da malignità di coloro che hanno a diliberare

episodes.description: In the Latin council the praetor Annius urged deciding what to do rather than what to say, since words are easily fitted once plans are unfolded.
episodes.quote: Ad summam rerum nostrarum pertinere arbitror, ut cogitetis magis, quid agendum nobis, quam quid loquendum sit

episodes.description: After Hieronymus's death Syracuse hung divided between Rome and Carthage until Apollonides's prudent oration showed that the ambiguity itself, not either choice, would ruin the republic.
episodes.quote: Apollonide, uno de’ primi in Siracusa, con una sua orazione piena di prudenza

episodes.description: The Lavinians delayed aiding the Latins so long that as they marched out the gate news came of the Latin defeat, prompting the praetor Milionius's remark that the short march would cost them dear with Rome.
episodes.quote: Questo poco della via ci costerà assai col Popolo romano

episodes.description: The Florentines delayed ratifying the neutrality accord with Louis XII during his descent against Ludovico Sforza; the late ratification was refused, costing Florence much money and nearly the state.
episodes.quote: Fu differita tale ratificazione da chi per poca prudenza favoriva le cose di Lodovico

notes: Machiavelli adds that such ambiguity has repeatedly damaged 'la republica nostra' (Florence).

heading_en: How far the soldiers of our times diverge from the ancient orders
thesis: Modern armies, having abandoned the Roman three-line order that let an army rally three times in battle, stake everything on the first shock and can be ruined by any small disorder.
thesis_quote: chi si ordina di potersi rifare nelle giornate tre volte, ha ad avere tre volte inimica la fortuna a volere perdere, ed ha ad avere per iscontro una virtù che sia atta tre volte a vincerlo

propositions.statement: Victory consists in obstinacy of spirit: while it lasts in the breasts of the fighters, armies never turn.
propositions.quote: nella quale ostinazione consiste, come altre volte si è detto, la vittoria; perché, mentre che la dura ne’ petti di quelli che combattono, mai non dànno volta gli eserciti

propositions.statement: An army that stands only on the first shock, as all Christian armies now do, can easily lose, since any disorder or middling virtue can snatch victory from it.
propositions.quote: chi non sta se non in sul primo urto, come stanno oggi tutti gli eserciti cristiani, può facilmente perdere; perché ogni disordine, ogni mezzana virtù gli può tôrre la vittoria

propositions.statement: Modern deployments in which lines cannot receive one another make the ranks crash together, so that a minimal accident ruins an army.
propositions.quote: urtando la prima la seconda, e la seconda la terza, ne nasce tanta confusione, che spesso un minimo accidente rovina uno esercito

episodes.description: Rome's most important battle ever, against the Latins in the consulship of Torquatus and Decius, with armies equal in order, virtue, obstinacy and number, Livy giving the edge only to the Roman commanders; Livy's account also sets out the hastati-principes-triarii order.
episodes.quote: fu questa che ei fece con i popoli latini, nel consolato di Torquato e di Decio

episodes.description: To hold their soldiers firm and resolved, one consul killed himself (Decius's devotio) and the other his own son (Torquatus).
episodes.quote: di due Consoli, per tenere fermi gli animi de’ soldati, ed ubbidienti a’ comandamenti loro, e diliberati al combattere l’uno ammazzò sé stesso, e l’altro il figliuolo

episodes.description: At the battle of Ravenna, where Gaston de Foix died, both the Spanish and French armies deployed all their troops in a single wide shallow front.
episodes.quote: Gli eserciti spagnuoli e franciosi nella zuffa di Ravenna, dove morì monsignor de Fois capitano delle genti di Francia

episodes.description: At San Regolo and elsewhere in the Pisan war the Florentines were routed when their own repulsed cavalry crashed into their infantry, as the veteran captain Ciriaco dal Borgo often affirmed to Machiavelli.
episodes.quote: non nacque tale rovina d’altronde che dalla cavalleria amica; la quale, sendo davanti e ributtata da’ nimici, percosse nella fanteria fiorentina

episodes.description: The Swiss, masters of modern war, take care above all when serving with the French to place themselves where friendly cavalry, if repulsed, cannot crash into them.
episodes.quote: I Svizzeri, che sono i maestri delle moderne guerre, quando ei militano con i Franciosi, sopra tutte le cose hanno cura di mettersi in lato

notes: Episode 2 spans Livy 8.7 (execution of Torquatus's son) and 8.9 (Decius's devotio); 8:9 given for the devotio mentioned first.

heading_en: How much artillery should be esteemed by armies in the present times
thesis: Artillery is useful to an army in which the ancient virtue is mingled, but against a virtuous army it is quite useless by itself; it helps the attacker far more than the defender, and the Romans would have conquered even faster with it.
thesis_quote: l’artiglieria essere utile in uno esercito quando vi sia mescolata l’antica virtù; ma, sanza quella, contro a uno esercito virtuoso è inutilissima

propositions.statement: Artillery does incomparably more harm to the defender than to the attacker.
propositions.quote: io credo che sanza comparazione faccino più danno a chi si difende, che a chi offende

propositions.statement: It is a maxim that where men can go in a mass and with impetus, artillery does not hold them.
propositions.quote: questa è una massima, che dove gli uomini in frotta e con impeto possono andare, le artiglierie non gli sostengono

propositions.statement: Since Rome's wars were almost all offensive, the Romans would have had more advantage and made their conquests faster had artillery existed then.
propositions.quote: quelli arebbono avuto più vantaggio, e più presto arebbono fatto i loro acquisti, se le fossono state in quelli tempi

propositions.statement: Infantry can evade artillery fire more easily than ancient infantry evaded elephants and scythed chariots, since artillery hinders only before the fight, not during it.
propositions.quote: con più facilità le fanterie, nello accostarsi al nimico, possono fuggire il colpo delle artiglierie, che non potevano anticamente fuggire l’impeto degli elefanti

episodes.description: At Brescia, Gaston de Foix dismounted and led his squadron through the whole Venetian artillery lining the street from the fortress and took the city without notable harm.
episodes.quote: quello con il suo squadrone, disceso a piede, passando per il mezzo di quelle, occupò la città

episodes.description: At Ravenna the Spaniards, entrenched between the Ronco and a too-low rampart, were forced by the French artillery to leave their defenses and come to battle.
episodes.quote: furono costretti dalle artiglierie uscire delle fortezze loro, e venire alla zuffa

episodes.description: At Novara in 1513 the Swiss, without artillery or cavalry, attacked the French army entrenched with artillery and broke it without hindrance from the guns.
episodes.quote: i quali a Novara nel 1513, sanza artiglierie e sanza cavagli, andarono a trovare lo esercito francioso, munito d’artiglierie, dentro alle fortezze sue, e lo roppono

episodes.description: In twenty-four years of Italian wars only count Lodovico della Mirandola at Ferrara and the duke of Nemours at Cerignola died by artillery; Foix at Ravenna died by steel.
episodes.quote: dal conte Lodovico della Mirandola, che morì a Ferrara quando i Viniziani, pochi anni sono, assaltarono quello stato, ed il Duca di Nemors, che morì alla Cirignuola, in fuori

episodes.description: The Turk's artillery victories over the Sophi and the Soldan came only from the unaccustomed noise frightening their cavalry.
episodes.quote: se il Turco, mediante l’artiglieria, contro al Sofi ed il Soldano ha avuto vittoria

notes: Ottoman victories (Chaldiran, Marj Dabiq era) tagged contemporary-italy for period as 1500s events; no closer enum value.
